summary: Round r1 (restricted network). No values retrieved; all empirical items pending. Health financing will come from Nepal National Health Accounts (MoHP, tier 1) with WHO GHED kept separately; catastrophic spending (SDG 3.8.2) from WHO and own computation on NLSS IV microdata. Province-level health-worker density requires MoHP/DoHS filled-position data by cadre and province over 10C population denominators; WHO NHWA is national only and council registrations are not an active-workforce measure. Stunting trend from NDHS 2001-2022 (WHO 2006 standards) with the JME series as cross-check; its labour-productivity implication is defined as a cohort-weighted labour-quality adjustment to 2070 using literature elasticities as labelled assumptions. Sixteen leads: four shared, three catalog endpoints, nine general-knowledge URLs marked unverified.

findings.claim: Q1: Current health expenditure (CHE) as percent of GDP and per capita; out-of-pocket (OOP) expenditure as percent of CHE, from the latest Nepal National Health Accounts.
findings.note: Required: NHA report tables (10A-L01). Record NHA round, FY coverage and SHA 2011 basis.

findings.claim: Q1: CHE and OOP share of CHE from WHO GHED.
findings.note: Separate observation; GHED year label vs Nepal FY mapping must be read from GHED metadata; may re-estimate NHA gaps.
findings.period: GHED year label (mapping to FY pending)

findings.claim: Q1: Catastrophic health spending - share of population with household health spending above 10 percent and above 25 percent of total household consumption (SDG 3.8.2).
findings.note: WHO GHO published value (survey-year based) and own computation from NLSS IV microdata; keep both.
findings.period: survey year (NLSS III 2010/11 or IV 2022/23 as used)

findings.claim: Q1: Health spending by government tier (federal, provincial, local) post-federalisation.
Q2: Health-worker density (doctors, nurses/midwives, other cadres) per 10,000 population, national, WHO NHWA/GHO.
findings.note: Unit ratio expressed per 10,000 population (stated in claim). National only unless MoHP reports provinces.

findings.claim: Q2: Health-worker density per 10,000 population by province (seven provinces).
findings.note: Numerator: MoHP/DoHS filled positions by cadre and province, or HRH profile; denominator: 10C province population (census 2021 or NSO projection, stated). Public-sector only unless private staffing tables exist; NHFS 2021 covers sampled facilities only.

findings.claim: Q2: Registered vs active workforce gap and health-worker emigration (nurses in OECD countries).
findings.note: Council registrations are cumulative and include emigrants/retirees; OECD IMO chapter for emigrant stock.

findings.claim: Q3: Under-5 stunting prevalence, national and by province, NDHS 2001, 2006, 2011, 2016, 2022 (and MICS 2019 separately).
findings.note: Required: NDHS reports (10A-L06, 10A-L07). WHO 2006 standards for all rounds (earlier rounds re-analysed); JME harmonised series as cross-check (10A-L08).

findings.claim: Q3: Implied effect of stunting on future labour productivity - cohort-weighted share of the working-age population that was stunted in childhood, 2025-2070, and the associated adult-productivity penalty.
findings.note: Estimate to be built from stunting trend (by birth cohort), 10C age-structure paths and a literature productivity elasticity (HCI method, 10A-L09; Hoddinott et al., 10A-L10) entered as a labelled assumption. No elasticity value recorded in r1.

findings.claim: Nepal National Health Accounts (tier 1) is the default for health-financing levels; WHO GHED is kept as a separate observation and differences are classified (vintage, year mapping, re-estimation) per 00B.
Registered health workers (council registrations) are not a measure of the active workforce and are never used as a density numerator.

Stunting affects labour productivity only through the cohorts that enter working age; the channel is lagged by roughly the age at labour-market entry, so current stunting affects productivity mostly after the mid-2030s. Elasticities from the literature are labelled assumptions, not Nepal-specific estimates.

data_gaps: Latest NHA round and its FY coverage not confirmed; document URL not located (catalog landing page only).
Province-level health-worker counts by cadre, including the private sector, may not be published; public filled positions are the likely only source.
Active (practising) workforce vs registrations unknown; emigration of nurses only partly visible through OECD data.
Catastrophic spending for FY2022/23 requires NLSS IV microdata access (registration may be needed).
Nepal-specific estimates of the stunting-productivity link not located; literature elasticities are cross-country.

assumptions.text: NHA is the default for financing levels; GHED is a separate observation; differences classified per 00B.
Density numerators use active/filled positions, never cumulative registrations.
Stunting enters the economic model only as a lagged, cohort-weighted labour-quality adjustment with literature-range elasticities labelled as assumptions.
Health spending is reported against the welfare objectives (financial protection, health outcomes), not only as a GDP input; trade-offs reported via src/economic_model/welfare.py.

challenges.text: Share one observation set for health spending by government tier (lead 10A-L11 is also used by 11C) to avoid double ingestion and inconsistent FY mapping.

Human-capital adjustment in growth accounting should not double count: if PWT hc (schooling-based) is used, the stunting adjustment is an addition only if its channel (health/cognition) is argued separately.
OECD IMO 2025 health-professional migration chapter is relevant to Nepal's own workforce density, not only destination demand; please flag Nepal-origin nurse data when ingested.

uncertainty: High for r1. Financing shares depend on NHA round and GHED re-estimation; OOP may differ materially between sources due to year mapping and treatment of informal payments. Province densities are uncertain because private-sector staffing and dual practice are poorly recorded. The stunting-productivity link rests on cross-country elasticities with wide ranges; its size for Nepal is not estimated in r1. Nine of sixteen lead URLs are general knowledge and unverified.

cadres: community health workers (FCHVs reported separately, not counted as health workers)

productivity_link.method: Map stunting prevalence by birth cohort onto the 10C age structure to obtain the share of the working-age population stunted in childhood each year to 2070; apply a literature adult-productivity penalty (labelled assumption, ranges from 10A-L09/10A-L10) to derive an aggregate labour-quality adjustment for 01A.
